note: The Magyar migration into Pannonia (895–896) brought the Hungarian tribes into direct conflict with the First Bulgarian Empire, whose Khan Simeon I had been raiding Byzantine territory. A Byzantine-Magyar alliance attacked Bulgaria from the north while Byzantine forces pressed from the south (894–896). Simeon defeated the Magyars in the counterattack, killing their prince Liutold; he then made peace with Byzantium. The Magyar-Bulgarian conflict shaped the early history of both peoples: it contributed to the Magyar migration further west into the Carpathian Basin and gave Simeon the free hand to pursue his Byzantine-focused imperial ambitions.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Magyar-Bulgarian conflict demonstrates the interconnected nature of 9th-century steppe and Balkan politics; Byzantine use of Magyars against Bulgaria models the great power's technique of deploying steppe peoples against Balkan rivals; the conflict's outcome shapes both Magyar settlement patterns and Bulgarian imperial ambitions
